fields.v: Google, USA (Sunnyvale CA: Dong; Kirkland WA: Shi, Sampath, Macvean)

Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — qualitative content analysis of 91 enterprise agent rule files, yielding a normative taxonomy of desirable agent behaviours (4 expectations / 15 attributes) as a basis for evaluations beyond correctness
fields.why: Format corrected to '<main>; secondary: <x> — detail'. Main nature is a judgement: the stated main contribution is the taxonomy, framed as vocabulary for designing evaluations (p 1, 4), so 'Proposes an evaluation method' as main is also defensible; no tool is evaluated, only rule documents analysed.

fields.v: Agent rules: project-level rule/configuration files for coding agents (e.g., CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md) as deployed internally at Google; no version

Project-level rule file with custom instructions and behavioural guidelines steering how the agent approaches tasks in a codebase. Observed content per taxonomy: 1 Adhere to Standards and Processes (best practices, project workflows/conventions); 2 Ensure Code Quality and Reliability (style, readable/maintainable, robust/performant); 3 Solve Problems Effectively (understand context, work incrementally, validate proactively, task focus, infer intent, learn by example); 4 Collaborate with the Developer (communicate, seek help, plan collaboratively and analyse trade-offs, learn from feedback, e.g., lessons_learned.md)
Not stated (no flow prescribed); some rules ask for plan-before-execute and incremental change-then-test
Not stated as a method; observed rules require plans/recommendations presented for developer approval and pausing to defer to the developer under ambiguity or high stakes
